payload.name: hol-rulebook
payload.problem_domain: Heroes of Legend TTRPG rulebook chapter review and disposition

payload.statement:
Chapter under review: ch18 (quarto-book/chapters/18-advancement.qmd), "Advancement", 183 lines.

Task: audit the chapter as a publishable unit and produce a disposition plan.
Each member audits through their own lens (see role card) and files a finding:
  stance support = the chapter holds on this lens as written
  stance refute  = the chapter must change; name the fix and its scope
Findings cite [file:line] in the chapter (18-advancement.qmd). Mechanics
findings state the broken value and the expected value. Cross-chapter checks
use the authoritative chapters as the reference, not this chapter (core
rules = ch06; combat = ch13: conditions, one-roll principle, modifiers;
disciplines/economy = ch08: DP, ladder, progression; classes = ch05: the nine
classes and their names; attributes = ch03: the -2 to +2 ceiling; skills =
ch07: skill roster and costs; faction system = ch19: @sec-faction-system,
faction actions incl. the Train and Fortify Position actions; bestiary = ch20:
Guard/Bandit stat blocks, @sec-chapter-bestiary; attitudes = ch14: the
Hostile/Neutral/Friendly/Allied ladder; glossary = ch21; reference tables =
ch22).

Disposition classes (for the librarian's synthesis):
  mechanical    - safe to implement as a micro-PR (headings, tables, wording,
                  em-dashes, single-cell refs, budget rows, worked-example
                  arithmetic that is canon-determined by another chapter)
  substantive   - needs a dispatched implementation pass (multi-file, new
                  content, worked-example rewrite requiring new narrative)
  design-decision - needs Bruce's ruling; implement the recommended default,
                  flagged veto-revertible in decisions-pending.md

Standing book conventions are in force: zero em-dashes in book text; damage
budgets flat at Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21; card costs 2/4/8
DP (rank 1/2/3 of skills, talents, and abilities); Adept prereqs exactly 2,
Master exactly 3; no flat +N damage riders anywhere in the book (a damage
bonus must be a budget row, a Basic-card floor of 1/2/3 + attribute, or a
"+1 damage tier" bump - titles and stronghold benefits included); one-roll
principle (the hit or casting roll IS the outcome, no second damage roll);
damage dice are dead outside the allowed random-table exceptions (1d4/1d6
random behavior, 1d4+1 duration dice); attribute ceiling -2 to +2; class
names are exactly the nine from ch05 (Protector, Blade, Arcanist, Shepherd,
Intellect, Odd, Leader, Unbalanced, Shadow - "cleric", "wizard", "fighter",
"warlock" as class nouns are stale vocabulary). Violations of these
conventions are findings, not questions.

Scope note: this chapter is the canonical home for leveling, DP, reputation,
titles, retraining, and strongholds. Where another chapter contradicts it,
the finding should name BOTH files and identify which is canonical. The
council's output is a disposition plan; it does not itself edit the book.

payload.argument: Mechanics audit of ch18 finds four convention-breaking defects plus one retired class noun, each with a broken value and an expected value. First, the Dragonslayer title (18:86) and the Armory upgrade (18:175) both grant a flat +1 damage bonus, the exact rider form the book's zero-rider law bans on titles and stronghold benefits; both should be expressed as a '+1 damage tier' bump so damage stays keyed to the budget rows. Second, the Fortify stronghold action (18:141) says it stacks with the 'Fortify faction action', but the ch19 between-session action list names that action 'Fortify Position' (19:440), so the cross-reference points at a nonexistent name. Third, the follower trigger (18:146) demands reputation 'Allied (+3)' with a faction, attaching a numeric to a ladder ch14 defines purely ordinally as Hostile, Neutral, Friendly, Allied with no values (14:41-44); the parenthetical must go. Fourth, line 129 calls a party member 'a cleric', a class noun the book has retired in favor of the nine ch05 classes. The chapter's arithmetic holds everywhere else I checked: the DP column sums to the stated 32 with 4s at levels 1 and 5, attribute boosts land at levels 4 and 8 capped at +2 per ch03, Progression Disciplines sit at levels 3/6/9 and Adept/Master unlock at 3/7 per ch08, the retraining exchange matches the 2/4/8 card costs, every die roll is recruitment, treasure, or duration randomness rather than damage, follower HP 4-8 matches the Guard 8, Bandit 4, and Cultist 6 stat blocks, and the Train faction action reference is valid. No object-HP convention exists in the book that the stronghold +10/+25 figures would contradict.

payload.argument: Fact-check across all ten audit points: the arithmetic and economy checks hold (DP column sums to 32 with 4-point milestone rows at levels 1 and 5; three progression disciplines land at levels 3/6/9 exactly as chapter 8 prescribes; attribute bumps at levels 4 and 8 match chapter 3's wording up to the +2 maximum; the retraining swap uses two genuine chapter 7 skills, both Novice-tier at 2 DP, Intimidation keyed to Brawn; both referenced anchors resolve, and Bandit/Guard/Cultist hit points bracket the stated 4-8 follower range; Allied (+3) matches chapter 19's faction scale since chapter 14's attitude ladder carries no numbers; the Train action name and its non-stacking note are consistent). The chapter fails on wording, cross-referencing, and conventions: the Heroic (10+) trigger overstates the table's 10-14 band at both occurrences; the stronghold requirement of reputation 7+ with a faction is impossible on the -3 to +3 faction scale and sits below the table's Heroic-tier stronghold benefit; the faction action is called Fortify rather than its actual name Fortify Position; the Archmage title's free Adept spell contradicts chapter 8's discipline-gated Adept cards; flat +1 damage riders appear on the Dragonslayer title and the Armory upgrade where the book bans them outright; stale class nouns (cleric, wizard) survive in the stronghold section; and the Sanctum eligibility row names no class. The strongholds anchor itself is unique, and chapter 21/22 offer no competing title mechanics. Recommended dispositions: mechanical fixes for the (10+) band, the Fortify name, the reputation-7+ phrasing, and the retraining example arithmetic (canon-determined); convention fixes for the stale nouns and flat damage riders (mechanical per standing rules); design-decision for the free Adept spell title benefit and the Sanctum class-phrasing question.

payload.argument: Counter-example: at level 7, when Master abilities unlock, a player wants a Master-tier card. It costs 8 DP under the book's own card economy, but this chapter's largest level award is 4 DP and points are forbidden from carrying over, so that purchase is mathematically impossible; a 4-DP Adept card is only reachable on the two 4-point award levels (1 and 5). The forced-spend clause turns the residual 1-2 points per level into panic buys, and the once-per-level retraining swap (equal or lower cost, no refund) can only shuffle 2-DP cards sideways, never build toward or refund a 4/8-DP purchase, so the chapter's stated purpose of correcting early mistakes cannot repair the structural shortfall. The same no-cap pattern repeats: Reveling trades gold for reputation with no ceiling, letting money buy the reputation that gates titles, free spells, and followers; Fortify temporary HP stacks with the faction action and Reinforced Walls against a base stronghold HP the chapter never defines; the Armory and the Dragonslayer title carry flat damage riders the book's own conventions forbid. Disposition: mechanical, the fix is canon-determined arithmetic (either points must carry over or level awards must reach the 4 and 8 thresholds).

payload.argument: FRAMING: As librarian I weigh ch18 as a publishable unit against the locked book conventions and the brief's disposition classes. Ledger check: positions are empty, so this is a cold whole-chapter weigh; nothing to reconcile yet. (1) WHAT HOLDS: the section arc (levels, DP, reputation, reveling, titles, retraining, strongholds) reads in a teachable order; the DP table sums to 32 with milestone totals (3 progression disciplines, 2 attribute increases) matching the rows; the retraining worked example's 2-DP costs match the canon card costs; bestiary and faction cross-references resolve to the right chapters; stronghold upkeep is present with correct arithmetic. The skeleton is publishable. (2) WHY IT FAILS AS WRITTEN: one load-bearing economy defect — the per-level income stream with no carry-over can never fund the canon 2/4/8 card costs, so the top tier of the economy is unpurchasable and the forced-spend rule orphans DP on 3-DP levels — plus reputation gates cited on two unreconciled scales (7+, Allied +3, Heroic 10+), four convention violations (two flat +1 damage riders, a stale class noun, a misnamed faction action), and follower acquisition split across four uncoordinated channels. Seven items are must-fix before print (five mechanical, two substantive); the free-spell title benefit and the two-concept title model are Bruce rulings. Confidence is high because every broken value is arithmetic- or convention-determined by another chapter.

evidence.claim: 18-advancement.qmd:39,41-53: income of 3-4 DP per level with no carry-over cannot fund the canon 2/4/8 card costs — an 8-DP Master card is never purchasable, 4-DP rank-2 cards are unaffordable on the 3-DP levels, and each 3-DP level forces 1 wasted DP under the spend-every-point rule. Broken: economy cannot reach its own top tier. Expected: carry-over, larger milestone awards, or costs the income can reach. Disposition: mechanical (arithmetic canon-determined by ch08), must fix.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: DP don't carry over between levels, so spend every point

Broken: threshold floats between two scales. Expected: name the scale, or use the faction Allied (+3) gate the Followers section already employs. Disposition: substantive (cross-chapter scale reconciliation), must fix.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Reputation 7+ with at least one faction

payload.rationale: t-01 closed rejected 7-0 (unanimous refute, reject quorum 4 exceeded, no rebuttals, no impasse, no judge). All seven lenses converged on the same load-bearing defect: the chapter's per-level DP income (3-4/level, no carry-over) cannot fund the locked 2/4/8 card economy, making 8-DP Master cards categorically unpurchasable and 4-DP Adept cards reachable only on the two 4-point milestone levels (f-003/f-007) - a canon-determined arithmetic failure, disposition mechanical. The reputation gates cite three unreconciled scales in one chapter: 'Reputation 7+' (109) is unsatisfiable on the ch19 faction track (-3 to +3, Allied at +3) yet sits below the Rep table's Heroic (10+) stronghold row; 'Allied (+3)' (146) is the canonical faction-track value but needs the scale named; 'Heroic (10+)' (146, 151) overruns the table's 10-14 Heroic band into Legendary. The zero-rider law is violated twice (Dragonslayer title +1 damage at 86; Armory +1 damage at 175), a stale class noun survives ('cleric' at 129; 'wizard' at 120/125/174/180; 'rogue-ish' at 127), the faction action is misnamed ('Fortify' vs ch19's 'Fortify Position' at 141), follower acquisition runs through four uncoordinated channels with permanence stated only for Recruit (124/138/150-152), the Titles section never says how titles are earned and collides with the Rep table's Title column (68 vs 84), Group Reputation has no loss rule or DA guidance (mirroring ch19's structure), Reveling is a voice-flat stub whose +1 persistence is ambiguous and uncapped (78-80), stronghold HP bonuses (+10/+25) float on an undefined base, the Archmage title's free Adept spell bypasses the DP economy, the Secondary Stronghold Type example pairs a Keep with an upgrade (Library) instead of a type, hidden HTML comment residue sits at 56-60, 'priceless' is uncapitalized at 180, the upkeep base ('total value') is undefined at 183, and pagebreaks at 76/82 strand two near-empty widow pages. What holds (documented for the record, not re-flagged): DP table arithmetic (32/3/2), attribute cap +2 at levels 4/8, Adept/Master unlock at 3/7, retraining example (both 2-DP Novice skills, Intimidation keyed to Brawn), all four @anchors resolve, follower HP 4-8 matches Guard/Bandit/Cultist stat blocks, Train faction action reference is canonical, upkeep arithmetic (5% of 1,000 gp = 50 gp) holds, zero em-dashes, clean heading hierarchy, all six tables structurally sound.
payload.recommendation: Chapter 18 (Advancement) is REJECTED as a publishable unit on a single load-bearing economy defect and a cluster of scale/vocabulary/convention failures. Fix per disposition plan in ONE atomic ch18 PR: (a) DP carry-over: drop the 'don't carry over' rule so the 2/4/8 economy is fundable (canon-determined arithmetic; totals unchanged at 32); (b) reputation gates reconciled: 109 → faction Allied (+3) OR Group Reputation Heroic (10-14) named explicitly; 146 → 'faction reputation reaches Allied (+3)' with the faction-system anchor; 146/151 → 'Heroic (10-14)' (band-exact); (c) zero-rider law: Dragonslayer and Armory flat +1 damage → '+1 damage tier'; (d) stale class nouns: 'cleric' → 'Shepherd', 'wizard tower' → 'Arcanist's tower' prose + rename the Wizard's Tower stronghold type to Arcanist's Tower (implemented default, veto-revertible), 'skilled/rogue-ish' → 'stealth-oriented'; (e) 'Fortify' → 'Fortify Position' (canonical ch19 name); (f) follower permanence stated (table gains are permanent staff; Recruit grants temporary for one adventure); (g) Titles: section renamed 'Earned Titles', one sentence on how titles are earned (DA grants for legendary deeds), Rep table column 'Title' → 'Reputation Tier' (implemented default, veto-revertible); (h) Group Reputation gains/loss guidance added (mirrors ch19); (i) Reveling: story beat added, +1 persistence made explicit with a once-per-session cap (implemented default, veto-revertible); (j) stronghold base HP defined (50 base, +10 Fortify temp, +25 Reinforced Walls anchored - implemented default, veto-revertible); (k) Archmage title reworded so the Adept card is learned at no DP cost (implemented default, veto-revertible); (l) Secondary Stronghold Type example pairs Keep + Arcanist's Tower (two types, not an upgrade); (m) hidden comment 56-60 converted to a visible 'Why this exists' blockquote (book device, cf. Retraining); (n) 'priceless' capitalized; (o) upkeep base stated as construction cost; (p) pagebreaks at 76/82 removed so Reveling and Earned Titles share a page (verify via pdftotext); (q) comma-splice/agreement fixes (39, 183); (r) Sanctum eligibility names Shepherd/Leader. Design-flavored items (b-DP carry-over, d-Wizard's Tower rename, g-column/section rename, i-Reveling cap, j-base HP, k-Archmage) ship as implemented defaults flagged veto-revertible in decisions-pending.md.
